officialTitle: First-line crizotinib versus chemotherapy in ALK-positive lung cancer

design.blinding: Open-label; PFS by independent radiologic review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We conducted an open-label, phase 3 trial comparing crizotinib with chemotherapy in 343 patients with advanced ALK-positive nonsquamous NSCLC
design.notes: Crossover to crizotinib permitted after progression on chemotherapy.

clinicalQuestion: Is first-line crizotinib superior to pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy in advanced ALK-positive non-squamous NSCLC?

pico.population: Advanced ALK-positive non-squamous NSCLC, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
pico.comparator: Pemetrexed plus cisplatin or carboplatin, up to six cycles (crossover permitted)
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS by independent radiologic review. Secondary: ORR, OS, safety, PROs

arms.label: Crizotinib
arms.doseSourceQuote: to receive oral crizotinib at a dose of 250 mg twice daily

arms.label: Pemetrexed-platinum
arms.dosing: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5–6, every 3 weeks for up to six cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: intravenous chemotherapy (pemetrexed, 500 mg per square meter of body-surface area, plus either cisplatin, 75 mg per square meter, or carboplatin, target area under the curve of 5 to 6 mg per milliliter per minute) every 3 weeks for up to six cycles

publications.title: First-line crizotinib versus chemotherapy in ALK-positive lung cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Progression-free survival was significantly longer with crizotinib than with chemotherapy (median, 10.9 months vs. 7.0 months; hazard ratio for progression or death with crizotinib, 0.45; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.35 to 0.60; P<0.001).
Objective response rates were 74% and 45%, respectively (P<0.001).

Median overall survival was not reached in either group (hazard ratio for death with crizotinib, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.54 to 1.26; P=0.36); the probability of 1-year survival was 84% with crizotinib and 79% with chemotherapy.

safety.sourceQuote: The most common adverse events with crizotinib were vision disorders, diarrhea, nausea, and edema, and the most common events with chemotherapy were nausea, fatigue, vomiting, and decreased appetite.

strengths: Randomised phase III with independent radiologic review

clinicalImplications.text: Established first-line ALK TKI therapy over platinum-pemetrexed in ALK-positive NSCLC, making ALK testing a prerequisite for first-line treatment of non-squamous NSCLC.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Crizotinib is the historical comparator against which next-generation ALK TKIs (ALEX, ALTA-1L, CROWN) were tested.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 25470694.
